svg.text: ThreeDream
one deterministic simulation core, trained headless in Node, rendered by three.js, played in a browser
APPLICATION
seven live pages, the Unreal level runtime, a first-person match, training in the page
demo/
INTELLIGENCE
policy gradient with GAE, learned critic, MLP, Gaussian policy, replay, inference
tasks DriveEnv / ReachEnv / PursuitEnv: gymnasium-style reset, step, observe over typed fixed-size buffers
src/ai + src/envs
SIMULATION CORE
archetype ECS in chunked storage, fixed-timestep runner, seeded RNG, events, stable digest
deterministic: engine.step(n) in Node and engine.frame(dt) in a browser run the same simulation
src/core
PHYSICS
builtin: pure TypeScript, the reference solver
Rust to wasm: bit-identical, 2.6x to 4.9x faster
Rapier: a cross-check against a solver nobody here owns
src/physics + rust/
SCALE: WEBGPU COMPUTE
100,000 particles, 20,000-node soft bodies, WGSL
one refcounted GPUDevice shared with three.js
output blitted into the renderer's buffer, no readback
src/gpu
ASSETS
glTF reader and writer, Unreal .uasset packages, material graphs, PNG, RGBE radiance
formats are read rather than converted offline, so content authored in Unreal or Blender runs here
src/assets
RENDER
three.js, the only layer that imports it, so the barrel keeps a training run free of a renderer
src/render
IN THE BROWSER
WebGPU, WebGL2, wasm: rendered, interactive, where a trained policy is deployed
IN NODE
no browser and no GPU: headless training, 2,404 unit tests, every CI gate
One rule underneath all of it: the simulation is the only source of truth.
The renderer mirrors physics state into three.js objects each frame and never writes back, so the same scene trains headless and plays rendered.
